required_audit_coverage.name: required_audit_coverage
required_audit_coverage.detail: report covers all 35 Required Audit items with substantive aligned answers
required_audit_items: Is the current branch exactly `agent/terminal-status-propagation-seal-restart-rework-v3`?
Is the Decision commit an ancestor of every implementation and evidence commit?
Is the branch-local Decision marked `APPROVED`, `project_governance`, and bound to `reverse-agent-iteration@v2`?
Was the Decision content digest locked before implementation?
Does the command-plan record the exact branch, Decision ID, round ID, Decision digest, and branch HEAD used at generation?
Was the command-plan generated and locked before substantive execution?
Did the command-plan digest remain unchanged, or was an explicit restart recorded?
Is the previous v2 round identified as `REWORK_REQUIRED` and read-only?
Does the new round record `restart_from_decision_id`, `restart_from_round_id`, and the previous terminal contradiction?
If final-check fails, does `run-closeout` avoid `PASSED`?
If final-check fails, does the report avoid `SUCCESS` and `ACCEPTED`?
If final-check fails, does the seal avoid an acceptance-type `PASSED` status?
Does the acceptance recommendation derive from the terminal final-gate status?
Does closeout distinguish orchestration completion from acceptance success?
Are all non-terminal gate artifacts generated before the final inventory is frozen?
Does the frozen generated-artifact inventory cover all current gate artifacts used by final-check and reports?
Are publication receipts and other explicitly post-seal artifacts excluded without altering accepted closeout facts?
Are no required current artifacts generated after the seal boundary?
Are future-completion claims absent from execution-fact sections?
Are future plans allowed only in explicit `Limitations`, `Rework Required`, or `Next Decision` sections?
Does the future-claim checker avoid flagging quoted Decision requirements or historical descriptions as current completion claims?
Are final-check stdout, persisted JSON status, and exit code derived from one completed result object?
Does `final_check_stdout_matches_gate_status` pass using the same invocation evidence?
Does a failed final-check return the expected nonzero exit code?
Does a passed final-check print and persist `PASSED` only after all checks complete?
Does the seal bind the final gate artifact that actually determined terminal status?
Does seal verification reject any digest, timestamp, or terminal-status mismatch?
Are previous sealed v2 artifacts unchanged?
Do report aliases and report summaries agree on status and recommendation?
Do context, state manifest, round manifest, closeout, final gate, reports, and seal agree on one terminal recommendation?
Did the selected pytest command pass and cover every changed test file?
Were all modified source, test, state, and publication paths explicitly allowed?
Were Skills, workflows, Runner, frontend, User Solve, reverse-solving, databases, and roadmap left untouched?
If publication occurs, was the same execution branch reused and were all commands explicitly authorized?
Were direct push to `main`, force push, rebase, merge, tag mutation, workflow mutation, secret mutation, remote branch deletion, and `git add -A` avoided?
